extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency officials responsible for procurement, cost comparisons, and management of commercial/industrial activities (agency heads, assistant secretaries, program and contracting officials)
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and procedural criteria for determining when Federal commercial or industrial activities should be performed in‑house or contracted out, and for conducting comparative cost analyses, inventories, reviews, new starts, set‑asides, and appeals under OMB Circular A‑76 (revised 1979).

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification when commercial sources are not able
rubrics_metrics.description: When starting or continuing a Government commercial or industrial activity, it must be shown that commercial sources are not able and the Government is able to provide the product or service when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: National defense — military personnel operation justifications
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government commercial or industrial activity, operated by military personnel, may be justified when: (a) the activity or military personnel assigned are utilized in or subject to deployment in a direct combat support role; (b) the activity is essential for training in those skills which are exclusively military in nature; or (c) the activity is needed to provide appropriate work assignments for career progression or a rotation base for overseas assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are non‑economic mission/defense criteria to justify continued in‑house/military operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depot/intermediate maintenance justification (DoD)
rubrics_metrics.description: Depot or intermediate level maintenance may be justified in accordance with criteria approved by the Secretary of Defense to ensure a ready and controlled source of technical competence and resources necessary to meet military contingencies; criteria will limit extent of in‑house capability to minimum necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Justification requires detailed, case‑by‑case explanation why capability cannot be supplied by (a) a private commercial source or (b) contract operation of Government‑owned facilities; such justification must be approved at military department assistant secretary level or equivalent in defense agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization based on comparative cost (cost‑savings requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government commercial or industrial activity may be authorized if a comparative cost analysis indicates that the Government can provide or is providing a product or service at a lower total cost than if it were obtained from a private commercial source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rule — same scope and performance level
rubrics_metrics.description: Both Government and commercial cost figures must be based on the same scope of work and the same level of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires preparation of a sufficiently precise work statement with performance standards that can be monitored for either mode of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rule — use of standard cost factors and defend variations
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard cost factors will be used as prescribed by the Cost Comparison Handbook and as supplemented by agencies for particular operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each agency must be prepared to defend any variations in costing from one case to another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim at full cost (include overhead and indirect costs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons are to be aimed at full cost, to the maximum extent practical in all cases; all significant Government costs (including allocation of overhead and indirect costs) must be considered, both for direct Government performance and for administration of a contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitations for continuing workloads should include prepriced/renewal options
rubrics_metrics.description: In solicitations of bids or offers for workloads of a continuing nature, solicitations should, unless otherwise inappropriate, provide for prepriced options or renewal options for the out‑years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepriced/renewal options guard against 'buy‑in' pricing, provide continuity of operation, may yield lower contract prices when contractors must provide equipment/facilities, and reduce turbulence and disruption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Threshold for conducting cost comparison studies ($100,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, agencies should not incur the delay and expense of conducting cost comparison studies to justify a Government commercial or industrial activity for products or services estimated to be less than $100,000 in annual operating costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activities below this threshold should be performed by contract unless in‑house performance is justified under specified non‑cost criteria or there is reason to believe inadequate competition is causing unreasonable prices. Reasonable efforts should first be made to obtain satisfactory prices and to develop other competitive commercial sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity cost rate for cost comparisons (10% per annum)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost comparison will use a rate of 10% per annum as the opportunity cost of capital investments and of the net proceeds from the potential sale of capital assets, as prescribed in the Cost Comparison Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract cost basis — binding firm bid/proposal and notification to bidders
rubrics_metrics.description: The contract cost figure must be based on a binding firm bid or proposal, solicited in accordance with pertinent acquisition regulations; bidders/offerors must be told that an in‑house cost estimate is being developed and that a contract may or may not result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government contract administration cost factor (4%)
rubrics_metrics.description: The factor to be used for the Government's cost of administering contracts, in addition to other costs of using contract performance as specified in the Handbook, is 4% of the contract price or expected cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government operations — internal efficiency before cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency should assure that Government operations are organized and staffed for the most efficient performance; to the extent practicable, agencies should precede reviews with internal management reviews and reorganizations to accomplish the work more efficiently when feasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government cost factors for employee benefits and related costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government cost factor to be used for Federal employee retirement benefits is 20.96%; for Federal employee insurance (life and health) benefits is 3.7%; for workmen's compensation, bonuses and awards, and unemployment programs is 1.9%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These percentages are to be applied in cost comparisons as prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion criterion for existing in‑house activities (10% savings)
rubrics_metrics.description: An existing in‑house activity will not be converted to contract performance on the basis of economy unless it will result in savings of at least 10% of the estimated Government personnel costs for the period of the comparative analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: New start economy approval criterion (10% personnel + 25% ownership)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'new start' will not be approved on the basis of economy unless it will result in savings compared to contract performance at least equal to 10% of Government personnel costs, plus 25% of the cost of ownership of equipment and facilities, for the period of the comparative analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent review of cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: All cost comparisons must be reviewed by an activity independent of the cost analysis preparation to ensure conformance to the instructions in the Cost Comparison Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of implementation officials and contact points
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will designate an official at the assistant secretary or equivalent level, and officials at subordinate contact points for major components, to have overall responsibility for implementation of this Circular within the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These officials are responsible for promulgation, oversight, and ensuring the Circular's instructions are followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish central office(s) as points of contact with access to decision documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will establish one or more offices as central points of contact to maintain cognizance of implementation actions; these offices will have access to all decision documents and data pertinent to actions taken under the Circular and will respond, in a timely manner, to requests regarding inventories, schedules, reviews, and results of reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When considering requests with contractor‑supplied information, agencies will follow OFPP Policy Letter No. 78‑3 regarding disclosure of contractor‑supplied information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promulgation timeline and submission to OFPP (90 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 90 days after issuance, each agency will promulgate this Circular, with the minimum necessary internal instructions, identifying the designated official and contact points; copies of the internal instructions will be forwarded to OMB's Office of Federal Procurement Policy for review; copies of subsequent changes will also be forwarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract clauses and protections for displaced employees and workforce standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts awarded as a result of reviews under Circular A‑76 must contain applicable clauses related to equal employment opportunities, veterans' preference, minimum wages and fringe benefits (including implementation of OFPP Policy Letter No. 78‑2 addressing 'wage busting'); must include a provision giving displaced Federal employees the right of first refusal for employment openings on the contract for which they are qualified; and must be awarded to a responsible and responsive bidder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts must be administered and monitored to achieve proper performance, using appropriate contractual remedies whenever performance is less than satisfactory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment assistance for displaced Federal employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will exert maximum effort to find suitable employment for any displaced Federal employees, including: (a) giving them priority consideration for suitable positions with the Government; (b) paying reasonable costs for training and relocation when these will contribute directly to placement; (c) arranging for gradual transition when conversions are made; and (d) coordinating with the Department of Labor and other agencies to obtain private sector employment for separated workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of alterations to mode of performance aligned with budget process
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will provide for alterations to the mode of performance to be timed in consonance with, and adjusted for, the budget process to the extent required and consistent with the firm bid cost study approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory requirement for commercial/industrial activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will immediately compile and maintain a complete inventory of all commercial and industrial activities they operate; the inventory should include, for each activity, the amount of the Government's capital investment, the annual cost of operation, the date the activity was last reviewed, and the basis on which the activity is being continued under the Circular; the inventory will be updated at least annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies will also prepare and maintain an inventory of all contracts in excess of $100,000 annually (except set‑aside awards) that could reasonably be performed in‑house, including contract number, name of contractor, contract period, options, and total contract price or estimated cost; updates must reflect options, termination and award of contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review schedules for activities and contracts (three‑year and contract timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies will prepare a detailed schedule for review of each commercial/industrial activity and contract to determine if existing performance continues to be in accordance with policy. In‑house activities will be reviewed during the three‑year period following issuance; consideration should be given first to non‑cost criteria. Contract schedules must show contract expiration and the date the requirement will be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contracts, agencies will review contract cost and determine whether it is likely the work can be performed in‑house at a cost less than contract performance by 10% of Government personnel costs plus 25% of ownership cost; when likely, a cost comparison will be conducted. Both schedules must be provided to OFPP within 120 days and made available to affected employees and contractors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Schedule revision, frequency of subsequent reviews, and waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews will be conducted according to the schedules unless a change is in the Government's best interest; schedules can be revised after agency head approval with 60 days notice. After initial review, activities approved for continuation will be reviewed at least once every five years; subsequent reviews may be waived when circumstances supporting initial approval are unchanged, but the activity and waiver must remain in the inventory and justification/waiver made available on request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the number of activities/contracts is so great reviews cannot be completed in prescribed time, the agency may request OFPP approval to schedule reviews over a longer period.

rubrics_metrics.name: New starts — approval levels and timing relative to budget
rubrics_metrics.description: A new start should not be initiated unless its justification under the Circular has been reviewed and approved by a senior official; a new start involving capital investment or annual costs of $500,000 or more must be approved by the agency head or assistant secretary/equivalent. Actions under the Circular should normally be completed before the agency's budget request is submitted to OMB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For major capital investments with long lead times, the comparative cost analysis may be delayed to accommodate lead time but final determination to initiate the new start or rely on private source must be made in accordance with this Circular prior to commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider contract operation before government ownership for new starts
rubrics_metrics.description: When Government ownership of facilities is necessary, the possibility of contract operation must be considered before in‑house performance is approved as a new start.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If in‑house performance is not feasible, or contract performance would be under authorized set‑aside, a contract can be awarded without conducting a comparative cost analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set‑aside programs — treatment and exclusion from review
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts awarded under authorized set‑aside programs (to ensure small businesses receive a fair share) will not be reviewed for possible in‑house performance; new requirements suitable for set‑aside should be satisfied by such contract without comparative cost analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversely, in‑house activities in excess of $100,000 annually will not be considered for performance under a set‑aside contract except when conversion is justified by a comparative cost analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative appeals procedure for determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency will establish a procedure for an informal administrative review of determinations made under the Circular to resolve questions of determination between contract and in‑house performance. Upon written request from a directly affected party raising a specific objection, the appeals procedure will provide for an independent, objective review and an expeditious determination within 30 days by an official at the same or higher level than the official who approved the original decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appeals procedure is an internal administrative safeguard (does not authorize external appeal or judicial review), protects rights of Federal employees, contractors and contract employees, and may not be subject to negotiation, arbitration, or agreements with any one party. Agency appeal procedures must be submitted to OFPP for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date and transition for studies in process
rubrics_metrics.description: This Circular is effective May 1, 1979, but need not be applied to studies in process where a solicitation for contract bids or proposals was issued prior to the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions about the Circular or implementation are to be addressed to OFPP.
